[spoiler=[u][b]For my claim[/b][/u]][i][u][b]1934-1939 The Battle of South Agros[/b][/u]

The battle began in August 1934, when the Larakyil Kingdom, ruled by the House of Faenir, faced an attack from up north by from full-scale invasion by the Oceanice Republic. Herichman Livake declared that all non-human was a deep threat and an enemy of mankind. Oceanice's industrial expansion into the Larakyil Kingdom saw it as a rich resource to grow on. King Faenir V Silvermane refused to submit to Livakes Human Purification Order and instead defended the southern world from total conquest.

The Oceanice invasion of South Argos began without a formal declaration. In late 1933, Oceanice armored divisions, supported by the naval fleet, crossed the Straits of Ervos and stormed into the northern shores of the peninsula. The Larakyil army was caught off guard, having underestimated the scale and speed of the assault. Within weeks, the border towns of Keryn and Velmor fell, their defenders overwhelmed by tanks and air raids. But rather than collapse, the Larakyil response hardened into a fierce, desperate defense. King Faenir personally organized the Beastguard Legions, composed of Larakyil non-human military forces and militias from the southern civilians to resist Oceanice expansion. 

From 1934 to 1936, the war across the South Argos peninsula was pushed back by the expanding military forces. Growing Pro-Humanist Fascism demanded to secure victory over land and the extermination of any non-human who rejects the Oceanic annexation. Civilians were massacred or deported, and the entire South was annexed by forces. The Battle for the Kelyric Highlands became the longest and bloodiest struggle of the campaign. The Larakyil used their experience and knowledge of terrain, striking by ambush during night raids, as well as ambushing columns and supply convoys. The Oceanic Republic responded with chemical smokes, air raids, and the creation of fortified clearing zones, which were open from barrage artillery.

By 1936, the war shifted to the Siege of Port Kelyra, the largest industrial hub in southern Argos and the Larakyil defense network. For sixteen months, the city was subjected to continuous bombardment from sea and air. The Oceanice navy, commanded by Admiral Velkir Drauss, imposed a blockade that strangled all supply routes. Despite starvation and relentless bombing, the Larakyil forces under General Seryn Vornclaw fought on, defending streets, factories, and hills that were important in keeping the fight going. When the Oceanice Republic finally broke through in mid-1937, nearly 400,000 soldiers and civilians lay dead, and the city was annexed and captured by the Oceanice Forces.

The final stage of the battle came with Operation Bervous in early 1938, Livakes directive to erase Larakyil resistance. New Silen-X rocket batteries were deployed to flatten the remaining highland fortresses, while the 3rd and 5th Oceanice Armies advanced in a two assault toward the southern coast. Paratroopers of the Skyborn Division captured the remnants of the Larakyil command network, severing communications and cutting off retreat. In a last act of defiance, King Faenir broadcast a message to his people from the palace's last defense.  Within weeks, organized Larakyil resistance collapsed. On March 27, 1939, Oceanice troops took Port Kelyra, signaling the end of the campaign and the complete subjugation of South Argos.

The Oceanice victory left over 1.3 million lives lost during the five-year campaign. Nearly half a million Larakyil civilians were killed or sent to camps. In the aftermath, the Oceanice Republic established annexation over the Southern part of Argos, transforming the annexed land into a military industrial zone under permanent occupation. Survivors of the Larakyil were rounded up into labor colonies and placed into a class system. The campaign was a long conquest of South Argos in the Great War of Reclamation. Larger genocide campaigns left many of Rukat species to face brutal camps and working conditions.

After the Larakyil Kingdoms surrender in late 1939, the Oceanice Republic swiftly occupied and dismantled the southern Rukat culture. The land was reorganized into six military zones, collectively known as the Southern Provisional Districts, which were governed directly by Oceanican authorities. Civilian rule was suspended, and the former kingdoms institutions were eradicated.

In 1941, the Species Integration Decree abolished Larakyilian identity and non-human citizens were reclassified as Subject Species, stripped of rights, and relocated into forced labor settlements around major industrial sites. Leftovers of Rukat identity and cultural landmarks were destroyed or converted to state facilities. While sacred relics were seized for ethno-scientific study. Larakyils vast mineral and gas resources were exploited to fuel Oceanices wartime industries. By 1947, the region supplied nearly a third of the Republics industrial output through brutal labor conditions.

Resistance movements, most notably Larak Eternal, waged a struggle rebels through the 1940s, culminating in the Highland Uprising of 1951. The rebellion was crushed through aerial bombardments and mass executions; over 120,000 anthropomorphic civilians perished in the fight for securing independent rights. The Southern Integration Act of 1958 finalized the annexation, renaming the land the Southern Human Reclamation Zone or S.H.R.Z. The Larakyilian language and faith were outlawed; education and public life were rewritten to glorify Oceanican dominance.

From 1960 to the present day, a huge transformation effort that led to Larakyils destruction became the foundation of Oceanices industrial and military power. Southern labor, resources, and infrastructure doubled national output by the 1970s, yet dependence on non-human workers under the racial system. Quiet reforms in the 1980s legalized limited rights for anthropomorphic technical auxiliaries, while mixed communities emerged across industrial towns. By the late 20th century, descendants of Larakyilian engineers contributed to Oceanican advances in aerospace and manufacturing.  Throughout the 1960s, the Southern Argos went into a full transformation of becoming part of today's OER.[/i][/spoiler]
